summary: [[character:riker]] and the new Bobs [[character:charles]] and [[character:arthur]] organize a rescue effort for the surviving human enclaves on [[location:earth]]. Their two-week survey finds about fifteen million people scattered among almost forty marked locations. [[organization:united-states-of-eurasia]] colony ships can carry ten thousand people in stasis, making the evacuation a fifteen-hundred-ship-or-trip problem, while HEAVEN vessels cannot land or enter an atmosphere. Scavenging autofactories are operating and a shipyard [[technology:autofactory]] is hoped within two years; Riker shifts manufacturing toward transport, and [[character:george-butterworth|Butterworth]] agrees that refugees may occupy his group's compound after its departure. Arthur begins outreach with manufactured communicators, but only about a quarter have been delivered or attempted and some groups resist contact.

Searching for mineral deposits with [[character:charles]] to support the rescue effort's manufacturing needs.

updates.state: Cloud and dust hide a surface scarred by dozens of asteroid and nuclear impacts that have disrupted the weather. A survey estimates that about fifteen million people remain in almost forty locations, with recovery taking five to ten thousand years.

updates.description: A converted interplanetary freighter equipped as a [[technology:von-neumann-probe]]: a small, light, resilient design built to copy itself. It carries a [[technology:surge-drive]] ring, fusion reactor, ramscoop, three large [[technology:3d-printers]], [[technology:roamers]], [[technology:nanites]] and mining cargo carriers, but no weapons. Version-2 HEAVENs add a larger reactor and drive, better reactor shielding, a rail-gun, [[technology:ship-busters]], bigger replicant systems and more cargo room. Its communications report to [[location:earth]] and were not built for interstellar conversation. HEAVEN vessels are not designed to land or enter an atmosphere.

A planned [[organization:united-states-of-eurasia]] colony ship designed by refugee scientists as an off-world refuge. Its plans require a space-based construction yard and a viable destination. It can carry ten thousand people at a time in stasis pods.
